title: Kernel fusion fragmentation and prefetch interference diary
content:
Purpose:
This is an investigative notebook capturing experiments targeting an observed tail-latency increase for mixed-length attention workloads. Hypothesis space centered on: (1) kernel fusion ordering and register pressure causing fragmentation; (2) prefetch scheduling interacting badly with paged attention (FlashPaged) under small-batch, high-concurrency scenarios; (3) fused op compatibility shims causing code-path divergence at runtime.

High-level observations to date:
- Regression surface is most visible on sequence lengths 64/256 mixed at 70/30 ratio with batch sizes 1–4.
- Single-GPU runs show periodic 20–40% p95 spikes despite steady throughput. Spikes correlate with kernel-switch events in traces.
- When fused attention+proj kernels are enabled, average latency improves, but variance increases.
- For paged attention, page faults/evictions are uncommon on big runs, but kernel rebinds (switching between paged and flash kernels) line up with microbursts.

Experiment matrix (short):
- A: baseline (no fusion, FlashAttention only), seq mix 64/256, batch 1..4, concurrency 16
- B: fusion enabled (attn+proj), same mix
- C: fusion + prefetch disabled
- D: fusion + prefetch aggressive (lower hysteresis)
- E: paged attention enabled (FlashPaged) with fusion on
- F: pinned KV cache + paged + fusion on
- G: quantized fusedops (8-bit accumulation path)

Representative commands used (internal harness):
- ./perf_runner --model gpt-small --seqs 64,256 --mix 0.7 --batch 2 --concurrency 16 --kernels flash --fusion off --prefetch auto
- ./perf_runner --model gpt-small --seqs 64,256 --mix 0.7 --batch 2 --concurrency 16 --kernels paged --fusion on --prefetch aggressive
- nvprof/run-trace: /opt/tools/trace_collect --pid <server_pid> --labels kernel-switch,kernel-latency,prefetch

Key raw measurements (median across 5 runs each):
- A (baseline): p50=42ms, p95=78ms, throughput=120 tok/s
- B (fusion): p50=34ms, p95=110ms, throughput=145 tok/s
- C (fusion, prefetch disabled): p50=36ms, p95=86ms, throughput=138 tok/s
- D (fusion, prefetch aggressive): p50=33ms, p95=160ms, throughput=150 tok/s
- E (paged+fusion): p50=45ms, p95=210ms, throughput=132 tok/s
- F (pinned KV+paged+fusion): p50=39ms, p95=96ms, throughput=140 tok/s
- G (quantized fusedops): p50=31ms, p95=130ms, throughput=155 tok/s

Interpretation notes:
- Fusion decreases median latency and increases throughput as expected, but p95 increases substantially in many configurations (B, D, G). That indicates fusion creates fast paths that are occasionally interrupted by heavy-cost events (kernel-switch or eviction).
- Turning prefetch off (C) stabilizes the tail relative to default, suggesting prefetch heuristics sometimes evict or reorder work, provoking kernel rebinds.
- Aggressive prefetch (D) made p95 far worse — likely over-eager prefetching overflowing scratch/private memory and triggering flushes/serialize points.
- Paged attention combined with fusion (E) had the worst tails; hypothesis: paged kernel has a different register footprint and its handoff to fused kernels causes expensive reallocation/copy.
- Pinning KV cache (F) largely mitigates the paged+fusion instability, consistent with the theory that occasional KV eviction/restore cycles coincide with kernel repatching.
- Quantized fusedops (G) improved median and throughput but still had tail events — costs likely from infrequent path that falls back to FP32 kernels for numerically sensitive sequences.

Trace-level signals we found useful:
- kernel-switch label (time, old_kernel, new_kernel) — look for repeated alternating switches around a burst window
- sm__inst_issued and sm__pipe_occupancy spikes at switch time
- memory copy ops (device->device) immediately before p95 spikes
- prefetch queue depth metric (internal telemetry) showing bursts that precede spikes

Short hypotheses to validate next:
1) Prefetch heuristics AND fusion ordering create transient register pressure that forces kernel epilogue specialization and full-register spills, slowing a small fraction of requests. Test: instrument per-kernel spill counts and run with explicit register allocation limits.
2) Kernel ABI incompatibility between paged and fused kernels causes a slow compatibility shim for boundary cases. Test: create a no-op fused kernel that preserves ABI and measure switch cost.
3) Small-batch high-concurrency workloads are sensitive to co-scheduling; combining high-concurrency with fusion causes contention on L2/shared mem. Test: run same config but limit concurrent sessions to 8 and measure p95.

Planned micro-experiments (next 2 weeks):
- M1: Add counters for register spill/store events across kernels. Low impact build. Owner: Ethan. ETA: 2024-02-16.
- M2: Implement a fused-kernel shim that avoids stateful rebind for paged->fused transitions. Risky; prototype only. Owner: Priya. ETA: 2024-02-23.
- M3: Prefetch hysteresis sweep: auto / off / conservative / aggressive. Owner: Maya. ETA: 2024-02-20.
- M4: Concurrency isolation runs on 8/12/16/24 to map p95 slope. Owner: Liam. ETA: 2024-02-18.

Temporary mitigations to reduce customer impact:
- Disable aggressive prefetch by default in hosted pool for affected model family until hysteresis tuning is validated. (Rollout ticket: jira/INFR-982)
- Add automatic fallback to non-fused kernels for requests exceeding a stable-switch threshold (seen >3 kernel switches in 100ms). This reduces peak throughput but lowers variance.

Open questions and unknowns:
- Are there driver-level scheduling interactions (CUDA/ROCm) that amplify kernel switch cost? Need to reproduce on both Ampere and Ada hardware.
- How often do these conditions occur in production traffic shape? Current sampled traces show the mixed seq pattern exists but frequency uncertain. Need longer-term sampling.
- Side-effects of disabling fusion on other workloads (LLM families with long sequences) unknown. Will coordinate with model-onboarding.

Attachments / artifacts to review:
- trace snippets (linked in linked_artifacts) with annotated kernel-switch windows
- flamegraphs of kernel time around a spike
- microbench harness code in PR at github link above

Action items (short):
- [x] Run M1 instrumentation and collect 1000 spike traces (Ethan)
- [ ] Prototype shim for safe paged->fused transition (Priya)
- [x] Prefetch hysteresis conservative rollout into a staging pool and monitor p95 delta (Maya)
- [ ] Concurrency isolation sweep and result upload to drive (Liam)

Notes to self (scratch):
- don't forget to compare with old attn-fusion-regression branch from Oct 2023 — there was a similar p95 symptom but with different root cause (tiling misalignment).
- cross-check with SRE for any correlating infra throttles (network, NVLink) around times of spikes.

Summary (one sentence):
Fusion helps median and throughput but exposes rare, high-cost events likely due to prefetch and kernel-switch interactions; pinning KV or conservative prefetch reduces tails — next step is low-risk instrumentation and a targeted shim to avoid expensive rebinds.

End of diary entry.
